analysis: Examined the base excerpt of .github/workflows/ci.yml (lines 529-893) and the head excerpt (lines 1-536), plus the incomplete patch excerpt. The visible change is CI-only and touches no provider code, wire protocol or cache crypto. It adds SAVE_CACHES, so only pushes to master or dev save caches and pull requests only restore. It adds CHECKOUT_SPARSE. It adds a five-step .git cache flow at ci.yml lines 61-94, 164-198, 227-261 and 467-501: restore the newest saved .git, discard it unless git fsck --connectivity-only passes, check out, and save once per day. It sets persist-credentials: false on checkouts, which reduces token exposure. Workflow permissions stay at contents: read. Actions are pinned by SHA. The fork-PR cache-poisoning route is closed for the .git cache because PR runs save nothing there; the cluster-metadata build cache is saved by a PR run only when nothing was restored, and that entry is scoped to the PR ref, so it cannot reach master or dev. A cache written by a master or dev push and restored into later runs is the remaining supply-chain trust assumption. fsck checks connectivity only and the checkout step then overwrites the working tree. The base excerpt shows the cluster and provider-test-gate jobs with expected-result checks that stay fail-closed. Threat-model relevance is indirect: T-041 and other provider threats are unaffected, and the release-integrity gate (ci.yml lines 107-132) still runs. Coverage limit: the head excerpt ends at line 536 and the patch excerpt is truncated. Head changes at roughly lines 660-1158 (shifted cluster, summary and gate jobs) were not visible, so I did not verify that the provider-test-gate and cluster conditions are unchanged in head. Later passes should confirm the gate logic still requires success for the selected lanes. No finding qualifies on the supplied evidence.
